title: _html_table zips body cells against `align` (not the row), silently dropping cells when align is shorter than a row
description: The body-cell loop is `for cell, a in zip(row, align):` (line 50). `zip` stops at the shorter of `row`/`align`, so the number of emitted `<td>` cells is capped at `len(align)`, NOT `len(row)`. If a caller ever passes a row with more cells than the supplied `align` list (or an `align` shorter than the header/row width), the trailing cell value is silently discarded — a column of data vanishes from the rendered table with no error. This is the opposite of the project's stated 'fail loudly' preference: a malformed alignment list produces a silently truncated table rather than an exception. The header loop has the same shape (`zip(headers, align)`, line 44), so a too-short `align` would also drop header columns silently. The correct contract is for cell count to be governed by the row width (e.g. iterate the row and default missing alignments to 'left'), or to assert `len(align) == len(headers)`.
evidence: Line 41 sets `align = ['left'] * len(headers)` ONLY when align is None. Lines 44/50 use `zip(headers, align)` and `zip(row, align)`. With e.g. row=['a','b','c','d'] and align=['left','right','left'], zip yields 3 pairs → only 3 `<td>` emitted; cell 'd' is dropped with no warning. All in-file callers (lines 101,108,116,141-145,172,237) currently pass align/rows consistent with headers, so the path is latent and not exercised by existing tests (tests/test_model_card.py only checks 2-column tables). `_html_table` is private (only used in this file), so the defect is a latent robustness/silent-failure hazard, not an active production bug.
